points.what: LATAM orders rose 36.9% WoW and contributed 41 of the week's order increase, 107.9% of the total change.
points.so_what: LATAM was effectively the sole driver of order growth this week, offsetting declines in other regions.

points.what: North America orders fell 4.0% WoW (contribution -8) and APAC orders were roughly flat, down 0.8% WoW (contribution -3).
points.so_what: Two of the four regions lost orders WoW, showing this week's growth was concentrated in LATAM and EMEA rather than broad-based.

points.what: Facebook and Display each contributed 15 orders to the week's growth, with Display up 41.7% WoW and 292.3% YoY, while Search, 68.4% of orders, was flat at -0.2% WoW.
points.so_what: This week's order growth came from smaller channels rather than Search, the core traffic source.

points.what: AOV rose to $89.50, up 7.9% WoW and up 9.3% YoY.
points.so_what: Rising AOV alongside order growth means this week's revenue gain came from both more orders and bigger baskets, not baskets alone.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.1%, up 0.9pp WoW (bad), though it is down 1.3pp YoY (good).
points.so_what: The WoW rise breaks the year-on-year improving trend, a pattern worth monitoring even though revenue this week beat target.

points.what: New signups fell to 251, down 3.1% WoW and down 3.1% YoY, while orders rose 4.5% WoW and 71.6% YoY.
points.so_what: Order growth this week did not come with new customer growth, since signups moved in the opposite direction on both a weekly and yearly basis.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue were both ahead of target this week, but YTD revenue attainment remains at 94.5%, behind target for the year.

points.what: Orders reached 889, 104.1% of target, and revenue reached $67,572, 116.6% of target.
points.so_what: Both weekly KPIs beat target, extending the quarter's ahead-of-target position, with QTD revenue attainment at 108.3%.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 94.5% versus target, and the current 8-week run-rate of $60,216 is below the $80,135 weekly run-rate required for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: Even with this week ahead of target, the recent pace is not enough to close the full-year revenue gap.

points.what: Revenue rose 11.6% WoW, a notable move at or above the 10% threshold, while orders rose 4.5% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue growth outpaced order growth this week, consistent with AOV rising 7.9% WoW, so bigger baskets added to the gain alongside more orders.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 23 Mar rose to 11.5%, up 2.2pp WoW, a notable and bad increase.
points.so_what: Rising returns are a quality risk to watch even in a week that beat target on orders and revenue.

points.what: Orders were 104.1% of target (889 vs 854) and revenue was 116.6% of target ($67,572 vs $57,958) this week.
points.so_what: Both weekly KPIs finished ahead of target, keeping the quarter's positive position intact.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 108.3% versus target, ahead by $9,863 with 11 weeks left in the quarter, while YTD attainment for the year is 94.5%, behind target.
points.so_what: The quarter is tracking ahead so far, but that has not yet closed the year's overall shortfall against target.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate of $60,216 is below the $80,135 weekly run-rate required for the rest of the year to reach the $3,888,802 full-year target.
points.so_what: Even with the quarter ahead of target, the recent pace is below what the full-year target requires.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 23 Mar rose to 11.5%, up 2.2pp WoW and up 3.1pp YoY, both notable and bad.
points.so_what: Returns are rising on both a weekly and yearly basis, a risk to order quality independent of this week's target beat.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.1%, up 0.9pp WoW, a bad move even though it is down 1.3pp YoY.
points.so_what: Each further point of cancellation is worth about $796 in revenue, so a continuing WoW rise is a risk to revenue.

points.what: New signups fell to 251, down 3.1% WoW and down 3.1% YoY, both bad, while orders rose 4.5% WoW and 71.6% YoY.
points.so_what: Signups are shrinking on both bases even as orders grew, a risk to future order volume if the pattern continues.
